subject: Re: Proposal — commitment tiers & swap safeguard
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@orchidhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@orchidhealth.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — commitment tiers and migration protection

Laura —

Thanks for the call earlier. We liked the perf profile you showed. Procurement asked me to put the core asks in email so they have a record before legal digs in:

- We need a committed spend tiered discount structure that scales to 3 years.
- A short stopgap credit if our current vendor has a delayed data egress window (60 days).
- A clause that guarantees a fallback model (or cost cap) if latency degrades beyond agreed SLA during onboarding.

Can you send a worked example with numbers (commit tiers, unit price at each tier, and what credits/offsets look like during migration)? Also, procurement will want an explicit list of what Redwood will cover (onboarding engineers, data transfer credits, any integration work).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

Best,
Maria Gomez
Head of Cloud Ops, OrchidHealth

---
Attachment: orchid_current_usage_snapshot.csv (csv)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — commitment tiers and migration protection

Maria —

Appreciate the clear list. I’m attaching a worked example (pricing matrix) and a short draft of the swap safeguard we typically propose. High level summary here so procurement can scan:

- Commitment tiers: 12/24/36 month options. Example unit price per 1k tokens drops ~18% between Tier A (12m) and Tier C (36m) assuming baseline usage you shared. See attachment: 2026-07-19_orchid_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx
- Migration credits: we can offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 8% of the first-year committed spend (applied as billing credits). In parallel we can provide up to 40 hours of dedicated integration engineering for no charge.
- Stopgap (egress) protection: 45-day temporary credit trigger by default; we can extend to 60 days if Orchid signs a 24+ month commitment.
- Performance safeguard: for the first 60 days after production go-live, if 95th percentile tail latency exceeds agreed SLA by >25% for two consecutive weekly windows, Redwood will provide an automatic monthly credit (formula in the attached draft). This is intended as a short-term safety, not a permanent pricing change — it also triggers a remediation plan.

Two asks from our side to narrow the draft:
1) Which commitment horizon is procurement leaning toward (12/24/36)? That determines how aggressive we can price the swap credits.
2) Can you confirm if any regulatory constraints force on-prem or VPC-only (we priced assuming hosted with VPC peering).

If you want, Connor can run a token-level delta to show forecasted monthly bills under both vendors (we have a quick script). Rishi included to confirm commercial approvals.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: 2026-07-19_orchid_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx (xlsx), swap_safeguard_term_sheet_draft.pdf (pdf)
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@orchidhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@orchidhealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — commitment tiers and migration protection

Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement reviewed your matrix and had two immediate concerns:

1) The onboarding credit at 8% is reasonable, but procurement prefers a hybrid package: 5% credit + 25% discount on professional services (PS) hours after the first 40 free hours.
2) The migration stopgap tied to a 24+ month commitment is a blocker for our CFO — they want a 60-day egress credit without forcing a term extension. If we can get that uncoupled (perhaps with a modest premium) we can move faster.

Also, legal asked whether the performance safeguard credit would be capped (they prefer a monthly cap at 3% of committed ARR).

We can be flexible on the commitment horizon if you can provide a worked example that keeps overall economic neutrality for our CFO (i.e., net present value of our current contract vs Redwood with the proposed credits). Can you ask Connor for a delta analysis comparing our current vendor spend vs Redwood under the three commitment tiers?

Best,
Maria

---
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — commitment tiers and migration protection

Maria —

Thanks, and appreciate the procurement flags. Quick responses inline:

- Hybrid onboarding offer: we can accept 5% one-time credit + 25% off PS beyond the first 40 hours. That gets you lower near-term cash flow impact and preserves our ability to staff the integration.
- Standalone 60-day egress credit: we can provide that if Orchid takes either the 24- or 36-month commitment OR accepts a small per-token premium of $0.0025 on the first 90 days of production. Alternatively, we can offer a staggered egress credit: full 60-day protection for 24/36m, or 30-day protection for 12m.
- Performance safeguard cap: we are comfortable capping monthly credits at 3% of committed ARR for the initial 6 months; after that we revisit during QBRs.

Connor — can you run the delta analysis Maria requested and attach a simple NPV table (current vendor vs Redwood for 12/24/36) and a blended month-by-month cash flow so their CFO can see the timing? If Maria confirms Orchid can provisionally commit to 24 months, we’ll produce a final term-sheet draft for legal.

Laura — I’ll approve the commercial concessions above.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
